_about: The demo video script. scripts/make_voice.py turns each line into speech; scripts/record_demo.py runs the steps in the real Switch room and lays the speech under the recording. Names in braces are filled in from this file and from what the room says.

lines.intro: Anyone can call their script GPTBot. The only real check is the address a request comes from, against the IP lists the AI companies publish. This Switch room runs that check as requests arrive, and drafts the report when something is wrong.
lines.room: This is a real Mattermost channel, connected through Switch. Two agents are members: egress-check, which checks addresses and logs, and abuse-writer, which drafts reports. A watcher follows our web server's log and posts each AI request here.
lines.spoof_send: First, I send a request that calls itself GPTBot, from my own home connection, to our test page.
lines.spoof_result: Seconds later it's in the room. The name claims OpenAI, but the address is in none of OpenAI's six published lists, and the registry says it belongs to my internet provider. The post hands the case to the writer.
lines.draft: abuse-writer drafts the report. The recipient is the abuse address the registry publishes for that network. The log line is quoted exactly, with its hash, and every list it was checked against is cited with its date. The writer can't send anything.
lines.ask: Anyone in the room can ask a question. Is this address really GPTBot?
lines.ask_result: The address is in OpenAI's GPTBot list, and the registry shows Microsoft holds it, so OpenAI rents it.
lines.approve: Only a person approves a report. When I reply approve, the writer records who approved it.
lines.approve_result: No agent sends anything. The person opens the draft in their own mail and sends it. This one would go to my own provider, so I won't send it.
lines.outro: The lists and registry answers in this video are real and fetched live. The code, the tests and the room setup are on GitHub, at the link on screen.
